We had intended to walk the entire perimeter, but I decided to skip the southern portion, as we were both getting dehydrated. We found more Bachman's Sparrows (Mia could hear three singing from one spot near the American Kestrel box), so there are probably several pairs onsite. We also found 7 adult Red-headed Woodpeckers (and heard several others), and we saw 2 Northern Flickers east of the powerlines. There were at least 4 American Kestrels along the powerlines north of the box, along with a female along the northern fenceline where the WEA heads north past the few homes. We left at 1349 and headed to Applebee's for lunch.

description: A solo visit to see what was around, and because I had not been out for eight days. Because of all the rain we have gotten the past few days -- and it is raining again as I write this -- I decided to avoid South Road and to stay on 3 Bridges Road and Gopher Road. As it turns out, I saw Julie Appleget on 3 Bridges Road and she said that she drove South Road earlier today. I did not stop along Rattlesnake Camp Road, so these records are solely from 3 Bridges Road (for its entire length) and Gopher Road. I saw very few nectar sources, so butterflies were pretty scarce; the only hotspot was a big clump of Tarflower, which attracted many swallowtails and one duskywing. I think I got two life moths if they get RGed. The weather at the start was sunny and 86 degrees ("feels like" 94) with a light breeze. I left at 1522, when the weather was sunny and 93 degrees ("feels like" 102) with a light breeze.
